title: Jubilant Argentinian Buckwheat Empanadas
description: A romantic Argentinian dish featuring buckwheat flour and double-rise bread, perfect for a lazy Sunday evening, this vegetarian-friendly recipe is a floral and creamy delight.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the buckwheat flour, warm water, yeast, salt, and sugar, stirring to form a shaggy dough.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover it with a damp cloth, and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour.
Punch down the dough and roll it out into a large circle, about 1/4 inch thick.
In a separate bowl, mix the ricotta cheese, melted butter, dried oregano, and beaten egg.
Spread the cheese mixture evenly over the center of the dough circle, leaving a 1 inch border around the edges.
Sprinkle the chopped parsley over the cheese mixture.
Fold the edges of the dough over the filling, forming a triangle or square shape, and press the edges together to seal the empanada.
Place the empanada on a lazy susan spinner and bake in a preheated oven at 375 degrees for 25 minutes.
Remove the empanada from the oven and let it cool for 10 minutes before serving.
